Hi Kenji — thanks for flagging this and sorry for the friction.

Short answer: Calendly normally converts to the invitee's detected timezone, but corporate calendars with forced timezone settings (or with attendees in a shared calendar using a different locale) can display the organizer timezone in the ICS payload. That’s the root cause here.

Workarounds we can do immediately:
1) Manual ICS in recipient timezone: I can generate a single ICS that is explicitly stamped as JST (we’ve done this before with APAC enterprise customers).
2) Two-invite approach: send one calendar invite in Redwood (CET) and a second, explicit JST invite for your team. The second invite is the canonical one to accept.
3) Quick video workaround: ask attendees to open the invite in Google Calendar web UI (top-right timezone picker) — unreliable but sometimes faster.

If you prefer, I’ll send a manual JST invite for Tue 11 Oct at 16:00 JST for 45 minutes and include a one-click join link. Monica, can you create the ICS and screenshot the calendar stamp? Ben — fyi, this is similar to the Finova case last quarter.

Diego
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
